notes:
Updates no longer need a Terminal.

- A copy that cannot replace itself now downloads the installer, checks it
  against the signed checksum, and offers to open it. Before this it said it
  could not update and stopped, and the only way forward was a sudo command.
- Installing hands the app to whoever installed it, so a fresh install updates
  itself silently from then on — a .pkg runs as root, and a root-owned app
  cannot replace its own bundle.
- The update bar says which of the two is about to happen rather than promising
  a quiet install it cannot do.

And the front page survives being resized. Below about 860 pixels tall the logo
went off the top and the drop zone off the bottom, and neither could be scrolled
to. It fits, scrolls when it has to, and drops the welcome furniture on a short
window so the folder list stays where you can reach it.
